title: Attestation and special reports — Whitfield & Co.
instructions: Whitfield & Co. (a CPA firm) receives the requests below. Select the most appropriate engagement or report feature, then identify the governing guidance for one request.

exhibits.title: Requests
exhibits.content:
1. A cloud payroll provider wants a report for its customers' auditors on controls relevant to customers' financial reporting, including operating effectiveness over a year.
2. A hospital system wants a publicly posted report on its data security controls.
3. A lender wants specific procedures performed on a borrower's inventory records, with the findings reported — no opinion.
4. A startup wants a CPA's report on its "what-if" statements assuming it wins a major contract, for use in negotiations with one investor.
5. A private partnership wants its tax-basis statements audited for its members.
6. A landlord wants an audit of a tenant's gross sales, which determine percentage rent.

parts.prompt: Select the best-fitting engagement or report.

rows.label: 1. Payroll provider — controls relevant to financial reporting, operating effectiveness
rows.explanation: SOC 1 addresses controls relevant to user entities' ICFR; Type 2 covers operating effectiveness.

rows.label: 2. Publicly posted security report
rows.explanation: SOC 3 is a general-use report on the Trust Services Criteria.

rows.label: 3. Specified procedures with findings only
rows.explanation: AUP engagements report findings without assurance.

rows.label: 4. "What-if" statements for one investor
rows.answer: Examination of a financial projection (restricted use)
rows.explanation: Hypothetical assumptions make it a projection, restricted to parties negotiating directly with the entity.

rows.label: 6. Tenant's gross sales
rows.explanation: A single element (gross sales) with materiality set relative to it.

options: Examination of a financial projection (restricted use)

parts.prompt: Which excerpt (paraphrased for study) explains why request 4 must be restricted in use?

excerpts.text: A financial projection is appropriate only for the responsible party and parties negotiating directly with it; the practitioner's report on a projection should include an alert restricting its use.
The auditor's report on special purpose financial statements should include an emphasis-of-matter paragraph that alerts users to the basis of accounting.
The engaging party should acknowledge that the agreed-upon procedures are appropriate for the intended purpose of the engagement.
The auditor should determine materiality for the single financial statement or specific element being reported on.

parts.explanation: Projections rest on hypothetical assumptions and are restricted to parties negotiating directly with the responsible party.
